[2] Control and profit share are different. An entity controls an issuer when its own voting shares plus voting shares held by issuers it already controls exceed 50%. Exactly 50% is insufficient. Repeat this rule until no new controlled issuers are found. The ultimate controller is a controller that is not itself controlled by another controller of the target. Profit share instead adds the products of share percentages along all ownership paths. No external agreements confer control. Unlisted shares are dispersed among unrelated investors, each holding less than 5%; they do not act together. Unlisted ownership links do not exist.
